description: Committee recommends 3% annual funding increases and $100,000 bonus for Discover Saskatoon.
Also recommends $50,000 annual increase to the special events reserve.
Recommends exploring governance reforms for tourism agencies.

chips.text: Administration believes efficiencies exist in combining agencies, despite Discover's view.
Saskatoon taxpayers may fund increased tourism agency contributions.
Administration could not explain why Saskatoon never ranked first in hotel metrics.
Hotel industry urged stable funding, citing substantial investment in Discover Saskatoon.
Competition Bureau directive impacted Marriott hotels' participation in voluntary funding.
Administration will explore governance reforms for tourism agencies by Q3 2026.

segments.title: Administration presents tourism funding report
segments.takeaway: Administration presented its report on tourism agency funding, recommending a performance-based structure for Discover Saskatoon starting in 2027.

segments.title: Discover Saskatoon Chair's presentation
segments.takeaway: Joan Stecken, Chair of Discover Saskatoon, argued against amalgamating with SREEDA and clarified that bid incentive funding is not part of Discover Saskatoon's operating budget.

segments.title: Hotel owners advocate for stable civic investment
segments.takeaway: Vanessa Costa Roskeh, representing Saskatoon's hotel owners, emphasized their consistent investment in Discover Saskatoon and the need for stable civic funding to share responsibility for demand gener

segments.title: Discover Saskatoon CEO's presentation
segments.takeaway: Stephanie Pocha, CEO of Discover Saskatoon, detailed the organization's role in driving visitor spending and clarified that special event grants are flow-through funds, not operating support.

segments.title: Questions on bid funding and SREEDA synergies
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned Discover Saskatoon's CEO about the special event bid funding, potential synergies with SREEDA, and the impact of changes to the Destination Marketing Fee.

segments.title: Questions on tourism support and mandatory fees
segments.takeaway: Councillor Ford questioned Discover Saskatoon's CEO about other tourism supporters, the voluntary Destination Marketing Fee, and the potential for a mandatory hotel tax.

segments.title: Questions on event bidding environment
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked Discover Saskatoon's CEO about the changing environment for bidding on major events and the attribution of visitor spending to their efforts.

segments.title: Administration clarifies funding and tax models
segments.takeaway: Administration clarified the comparative city funding, the accommodation tax models in other provinces, and the city's past efforts to lobby for a mandatory hotel surcharge.

segments.title: Councillor proposes alternative funding motion
segments.takeaway: Councillor Jeffries proposed a motion for a 3% inflationary increase, a $100,000 annual bonus, and a $50,000 increase to the special events reserve, sparking questions about budget implications.

segments.title: Committee debates and votes on funding increases
segments.takeaway: The committee debated the proposed funding increases, particularly the impact on future mill rates, and then voted on each item of the motion individually, with all items passing.

description: City begins process to amalgamate SaskTel Centre and TCU Place.
Goal is to complete amalgamation by early 2027.
Expected to save $470,000 annually by year three.

chips.text: Councillor Davies raised concerns about staff having to reapply for all positions.
Employees of SaskTel Centre and TCU Place are affected by potential job changes.
Administration committed to reporting to Council at least twice in 2026 on progress.

description: Committee recommends 3.9% electrical rate increases for 2026, 2027.
Increases align with SaskPower's proposed rates.

chips.text: Councillor Dubel questioned interim rates; staff cited increased electricity costs.
Staff promised a new report if the rate panel approves lower increases.

description: Reports 6.3.1 to 6.3.4 are now public record.
Sets April 16 by-election for St. Paul's School Division.
School division covers all election costs.

chips.text: Voters in St. Paul's Roman Catholic Separate School Division participate in by-election.

description: Refers Business Improvement District establishment to administration.

chips.text: Sask West Business Association proposes establishing a Business Improvement District.
